articles.title: Angel Reese's Dream to Host WNBA Finals Games vs. Valkyries at Hawks' Arena, New Schedule Announced
articles.summary: Games 3 and 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals will be played at State Farm Arena and not the Atlanta Dream's usual home, Gateway Center Arena.
articles.body:
Games 3 and 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals will be played at State Farm Arena and not the Atlanta Dream's usual home, Gateway Center Arena.

To facilitate the change, the league is moving Game 3 up a day to Oct. 21. The Atlanta Hawks are also pushing back their home opener to 8:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 24 to avoid any conflicts with Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.

There were initially fears the Dream would have to use Gateway Center Arena, a significantly smaller venue than State Farm Arena, for their home games against the Golden State Valkyries.

State Farm Arena is hosting a Sombr concert on Oct. 22 and then has the Hawks' opener two nights later.

At Gateway Center, far fewer fans would've been able to attend, and it simply wouldn't have presented a great look on television for an event as big as the Finals.

"Ensuring that Games 3 and 4 of the Finals will be played at State Farm Arena is an important moment for the Dream's players, fans, the organization and the city of Atlanta and is a testament to the extraordinary momentum of the team, women's basketball and the growing impact of women's sports," the Dream said .

This won't be an issue in subsequent seasons with the Dream moving into State Farm Arena full time beginning in 2027.

Under the old best-of-five format for the Finals, the Dream would've been assured of hosting at least one game. The WNBA adopted the best-of-seven structure starting in 2025, so Atlanta is guaranteed to have two games and potentially a third should the series extend to a Game 6.

articles.title: WNBA Finals moving to State Farm Arena for Dream home games 3 and 4
articles.summary: Games were set to be played at the Dream's 3,500-seat arena.
articles.body:
After several days of uncertainty and public outcry, the WNBA Finals Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta will be played at the larger State Farm Arena, instead of the Dream's usual 3,500-seat venue, the league announced on Tuesday.

The Dream played their first-round and semifinal games at the 17,000-seat State Farm, but Games 3, 4 and 6 of the Finals conflicted with previously scheduled events at the larger venue. The league changed the date of Game 3 from Thursday, Oct. 22 to Wednesday, Oct. 21, and moved up the time of Game 4, in coordination with the NBA's Atlanta Hawks.

The Dream and Hawks released the following joint statement:

"Relocating Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals from Gateway Center Arena to State Farm Arena was a complex undertaking that required extraordinary collaboration to navigate numerous challenges in a short time period. The Dream is grateful to the Golden State Valkyries, the Hawks, the NBA, the WNBA, and both league's broadcast partners. Without their focus and flexibility, this would not have happened. "Ensuring that Games 3 and 4 of the Finals will be played at State Farm Arena is an important moment for the Dream's players, fans, the organization and the city of Atlanta and is a testament to the extraordinary momentum of the team, women's basketball and the growing impact of women's sports."

"Relocating Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals from Gateway Center Arena to State Farm Arena was a complex undertaking that required extraordinary collaboration to navigate numerous challenges in a short time period. The Dream is grateful to the Golden State Valkyries, the Hawks, the NBA, the WNBA, and both league's broadcast partners. Without their focus and flexibility, this would not have happened.

"Ensuring that Games 3 and 4 of the Finals will be played at State Farm Arena is an important moment for the Dream's players, fans, the organization and the city of Atlanta and is a testament to the extraordinary momentum of the team, women's basketball and the growing impact of women's sports."

"We are grateful for the efforts made by numerous stakeholders, including the Dream, the Valkyries, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, and NBC Sports and USA Sports," WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said in a statement. "The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA Finals game to be played in the Atlanta market since 2013. We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action – the WNBA Finals – in person."

The Dream announced during the semifinals that they would play all 25 of their home games next season at State Farm , moving from Gateway Center Arena. But until Tuesday, it looked like their Finals games would need to be played at the smaller venue.

A Sombr concert is scheduled at State Farm Arena for Oct. 22, the original day of Game 3. The Hawks host Houston on Oct. 24, the day of Game 4, in their regular-season home opener, but the NBA team agreed to move the start time of their game a half-hour later. Unlike other WNBA teams, the Dream have no partnership or overlap with State Farm Arena or the Hawks. Their Finals opponent, the Golden State Valkyries, share ownership and an arena with the NBA's Golden State Warriors, and moved a Doja Cat concert to a contingency date to accommodate the Finals schedule.

The Hawks host Cleveland on Oct. 29, the day of Game 6, in the third game of the home schedule; the WNBA's statement did not address a possible Game 6 venue change.

"This is what the players and the fans deserve," said Larry Gottesdiener, Atlanta Dream majority owner in a statement. "We are grateful to all of the stakeholders who worked together to resolve the conflicts and make this happen."

"We are thrilled that we will be able to accommodate the Dream as they host Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena. Playing for a championship is special, and we want the Dream to feel the full support of the city during this amazing run," said Andrew Saltzman, president of business enterprise and chief commercial officer of the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena.

Due to the Game 3 date change, there will be only one off day (Tuesday, Oct. 20) between Games 2 and 3 as teams travel from San Francisco to Atlanta.

articles.title: Valencia Basket - Olympiacos en directo | Última hora de Euroliga en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Balón para Olympiacos. Rebote en ataque de Montero que hace que el Oly agote más segundos. Pero no hay canasta, aunque sí revisión de los árbitros. Na
articles.body:
Hola, muy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a la Euroliga . Si hubiera que elegir sólo un partido para ver esta jornada en la que se juegan siete, la mayoría de aficionados al balocnesto elegirían este Valencia - Olympiacos que destaca sobremanera en esta quinta fecha de la Liga regular . Es un partido entre uno de los equipos más en forma en este arranque de la competición, un Valencia sorprendente, y el actual campeón, el Olympiacos , algo menos regular, pero uno de los equipos llamados a pelear por estar en la Final Four.

En hechos, es el segundo contra el tercero. A ambos equipos les separa sólo una victoria, Valencia (4-0), Olympiacos (3-1) y estamos hablando de dos equipos que han hecho un gran baloncesto en sus partidos en la Euroliga . Sólo el Panathiniakos está por delante.

Además será el regreso de Jean Montero a la que fue su casa el año pasado, en la que cruzó la línea para entrar de lleno en la élite del baloncesto europeo. Un partido sensacional para saber dónde están los dos equipos ahora mismo y sobre todo para saber si el proyecto del Valencia es tan sólido como parece.

Con numerosos cambios (fue poco más que despellejado al final de la temporada pasada), el Valencia se ha reiventado de la mano de un Xavi Albert (que sustituyó a Pedro Martínez ) que decidió coger todo lo bueno del año pasado del Valencia y mejorarlo. Jugadores como TJ Shorts, Armoni Brooks, Nikola Mirotic o Mario Saint-Supéry han llenado de optimismo y euforia a una afición que vio como el proyecto peligraba tras el final de la temporada, pero que que siguen disfrutando de su equipo como si la campaña no hubiera acabado.

Enfrente, el campeón de la Euroliga del 2026 con los refuerzos de Codi Miller-McINtyre y Jean Montero . Con V ezenkov, Dorsey, Fournier, Ward o Joseph para conformar una de las mejores plantillas de Europa. Un partidazo que comienza a las 21.00 horas en el Roig Arena y que te vamos a contar en MARCA.com.

articles.title: Michael Jordan rompe otro récord histórico: pagan 14 millones por una camiseta suya
articles.standfirst: Es la cifra más alta jamás pagada por un objeto de colección relacionado con el baloncesto. El comprador, Ron Firman, inversor inmobiliario de Miami, orgulloso
articles.summary: Es la cifra más alta jamás pagada por un objeto de colección relacionado con el baloncesto. El comprador, Ron Firman, inversor inmobiliario de Miami, orgulloso
articles.body: Michael Jordan lleva más de 20 años sin jugar un partido de la NBA, pero su leyenda sigue batiendo récords. Una camiseta de los Chicago Bulls que lució y firmó durante las Finales de 1998 ha sido vendida por 14 millones de dólares en una operación privada anunciada por la casa de subastas Hunt Auctions. Es la cifra más alta jamás pagada por un objeto de colección relacionado con el baloncesto y una nueva demostración de que todo lo que rodea a Jordan continúa siendo oro. La camiseta roja corresponde al segundo partido de aquellas Finales, disputado el 5 de junio de 1998, cuando los Bulls derrotaron a los Utah Jazz para igualar la serie. Chicago acabaría conquistando el título en seis encuentros, el sexto y último anillo de Jordan con la franquicia. Una temporada legendaria que volvió a cobrar protagonismo mundial con el documental The Last Dance, estrenado en 2020, y que sigue alimentando el interés de los coleccionistas. "Aunque la importancia de Michael Jordan en el mercado de los recuerdos deportivos lleva mucho tiempo consolidada, ahora ha escalado hasta una categoría de activos de élite, más habitual en obras de arte icónicas", afirmó David Hunt, presidente de Hunt Auctions. La operación sitúa esta camiseta entre las piezas deportivas más caras de la historia: solo la supera, entre las camisetas de partido con un precio de venta conocido, la que vistió Babe Ruth con los New York Yankees en 1932, adjudicada por 24,12 millones de dólares en 2024. No es, además, la primera vez que una camiseta de Jordan de aquellas Finales alcanza cifras estratosféricas. Una de las utilizadas en el primer partido se vendió por unos 10,1 millones de dólares en 2022, mientras que otra del tercer encuentro alcanzó aproximadamente 12,3 millones el mes pasado. La nueva operación eleva todavía más el valor de una colección vinculada a la última temporada de Jordan en Chicago, convertida en uno de los grandes tesoros del deporte. El comprador, Ron Firman, inversor inmobiliario de Miami, no ocultó su satisfacción por hacerse con una pieza de semejante valor histórico. "Michael Jordan fue un jugador de un talento increíble, admirado en todo el mundo. Estoy muy ilusionado con la compra", aseguró. La camiseta había sido adquirida originalmente a los Bulls por un coleccionista privado en 2003 y, según Hunt Auctions, solo había cambiado de manos una vez desde entonces. En 2023, unas zapatillas Air Jordan que el mítico número 23 llevó en aquel segundo partido también alcanzaron los 2,2 millones de dólares. Jordan dejó las pistas, pero su leyenda sigue jugando en otra liga.

articles.title: El Kids&Us Manresa cede ante el empuje del líder Bahcesehir (100-88)
articles.standfirst: Allen (21) fue el mejor de los catalanes
articles.summary: Allen (21) fue el mejor de los catalanes
articles.body: El Kids&Us Manresa cayó por 100-88 ante el líder de la Eurocup, el Bahcesehir, en el Sinan Erdem de Estambul después de estar todo el encuentro por debajo en el marcador, con los turcos más acertados en el apartado ofensivo. Marcquise Reed, con 22 puntos anotados, fue pieza clave en los locales para llevarse el triunfo y dejar sin opciones de victoria a un Manresa que en ataque no jugó mal. Los turcos arrancaron el encuentro con la sexta marcha en el acelerador puesta, y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos firmaron un parcial de 9-0 de inicio comandado por Malachi Flynn para provocar el primer tiempo muerto de Diego Ocampo a los dos minutos de juego. El Kids&Us Manresa empezó a anotar en situaciones sencillas, pero los locales continuaron con su apisonadora particular en el apartado ofensivo, lo que aumentó un poco más la ventaja tras buenas acciones individuales de Marcquise Reed (20-10, min. 7). El equipo dirigido por Sasha Djordjevic se fue hasta los 15 puntos de ventaja, pero un triple sobre la bocina del primer cuarto de JD Notae dejó el marcador en 32-20 al final del periodo. En el segundo cuarto los catalanes mejoraron en ambos lados de la pista, y la picardía de Rafa Villar hizo que los suyos rebajaran la barrera psicológica de los diez puntos de desventaja para meter el miedo en el cuerpo a los turcos (36-27, min. 13). Los de Diego Ocampo tuvieron un poco de continuidad, y aunque los locales no bajaron el nivel en ataque, lograron rebajar aún más la desventaja tras unos buenos minutos de un Timmy Allen que le costó entrar en dinámica en este choque (45-38, min. 18). Los últimos dos minutos de primera mitad se convirtieron en un intercambio de canastas que benefició al equipo que ya estaba por delante, y el Bahcesehir se fue con un 53-44 favorable al tiempo de descanso. En la reanudación, al igual que en los cuartos anteriores, el Bahcesehir arrancó con una marcha más, y rápidamente volvieron a coger una buena renta tras otro triple, esta vez de Tyler Cavanaugh (60-49, min. 23). Sin embargo, cuando parecía que los otomanos podían escaparse e incluso casi sentenciar el choque, el Kids&Us Manresa mostró su mejor cara con un acertado Lukasz Kolenda y se pusieron a tan sólo tres puntos de desventaja (62-59, min. 26). Un espejismo, ya que poco después los locales volvieron a firmar un parcial a favor y acabaron con un 76-66 al final del tercer cuarto que no dejaba el duelo sentenciado, pero sí muy a favor. Ya en el último cuarto, los manresanos tardaron hasta dos minutos en anotar, lo que el Bahcesehir aprovechó a las mil maravillas para poner tierra de por medio y aumentar su ventaja (84-69, min. 34). El Bahcesehir, lejos de quitar el pie del acelerador, sentenció definitivamente el encuentro después de la enésima canasta difícil de Trevion Williams, que pese a ser un especialista bajo aros, anotó situaciones de todo tipo desde la media distancia (95-77, min. 38). Al final, el Kids&Us Manresa cayó en la pista del Bahcesehir por 100-88 para firmar otra derrota más en un inicio de temporada complicado. Lo más peligroso, otra vez el centenar de puntos encajados, como en la gran mayoría de derrotas hasta el momento. 100 - Bahcesehir Istanbul (32+21+23+24): Sipahi (3), Flynn (16), Mike (4), Cavanaugh (12), Williams (10) -cinco inicial-; Reed (22), Avramovic (7), Akpinar (-), Inglis (11), Haltali (-), Ponitka (12) y Mitrovic (3). 88 - Kids&Us Manresa (20+24+22+22): Benitez (11), Notae (8), Agbo (6), Allen (21), Ongenda (10) -cinco inicial-; Kolenda (11), Beaufort (2), Tamba (1), Fernández (3), Oriola (13), Villar (2) y Minchev (-). Árbitros: Milivoje Jovcic, Vassilis Pitsilkas e Ioannis Tsimpouris. Eliminaron por cinco faltas personales al jugador visitante Agbo (min. 35). Incidencias: Partido correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la fase regular de la Eurocopa de baloncesto disputado en el Sinan Erdem.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream to host WNBA Finals home games at larger arena after scheduling swap
articles.summary: The WNBA and NBA announced that after several logistical fixes, the Dream will host Games 3 and 4 of their WNBA Finals matchup against the Golden State Valkyries at Atlanta’s 17,004-seat State Farm Arena, rather than a 3,500-seat venue south of downtown.
articles.body: After the Atlanta Dream reached the WNBA Finals last week, the celebration was interrupted by a potential problem: Rather than play the championship series’ home games at the city’s large downtown arena, scheduling conflicts appeared to force them to be hosted at a tiny arena. On Tuesday, that scenario was avoided when the WNBA and NBA announced that after several logistical fixes, the Dream will host Games 3 and 4 of their WNBA Finals matchup against the Golden State Valkyries at Atlanta’s 17,004-seat State Farm Arena, rather than a 3,500-seat venue south of downtown. “The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA Finals game to be played in the Atlanta market since 2013,” WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said in a statement. “We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action — the WNBA Finals — in person.” Since 2021, the Dream have played its virtually all of its regular-season games at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena about 30 minutes south of downtown, the smallest home arena in the WNBA, by capacity. During this postseason, though, the Dream had shifted all home games to State Farm Arena, the home of the NBA’s Hawks, to an average attendance of 9,745. The location shift was a preview of a multi-year deal that will see the Dream play home games full-time at State Farm Arena beginning next season. After the Dream swept the New York Liberty to reach their first WNBA Finals since 2013 last week, however, conflicts immediately arose: a Sombr concert was set at State Farm Arena on Oct. 22, the date of Game 3, and a Hawks game was scheduled for Oct. 24, the date of Game 4. After multiple days in which the location of those games remained in flux, a fix was announced Tuesday that will keep the Dream playing in the larger, downtown venue. Game 3 will now be played Oct. 21, at 8 p.m. ET, one day earlier than initially scheduled. The game will air on USA Network and CNBC and stream on Peacock. Game 4 will take place still on Oct. 24, but will tip off at 1 p.m. ET as part of a double-header after the Hawks agreed to tip off their own game 30 minutes later, at 8:30 p.m. NBC will broadcast the game, which also will air on Peacock. (NBC Sports shares a parent company with NBC News.) One potential conflict remains, however: Game 6 of the series would be in Atlanta on Oct. 29, the same day the Hawks play a home game at 7 p.m. ET. “Ensuring that Games 3 and 4 of the Finals will be played at State Farm Arena is an important moment for the Dream’s players, fans, the organization and the city of Atlanta and is a testament to the extraordinary momentum of the team, women’s basketball and the growing impact of women’s sports,” the Atlanta Dream and Atlanta Hawks said in a joint statement Tuesday.

articles.title: Dream's Allisha Gray had procedure on injured hand; guard 'trending in right direction,' but status for WNBA Finals Game 1 uncertain
articles.summary: Gray told a local reporter that she had a minor procedure on the injury that's sidelined her since Game 1 of the semifinals.
articles.body:
With Game 1 of the WNBA Finals looming, signs are trending "in the right direction" for injured Atlanta Dream All-Star Allisha Gray.

That's according to Dream head coach Karl Smesko , who provided an update on Gray's health to reporters on Tuesday. But Smesko isn't sure if Gray will be available to play in Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries.

Game 1 is scheduled for Saturday afternoon at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

Gray was listed as a limited participant in practice Tuesday. She was seen hoisting up shots with tape around the injured fingers on her left hand, which is her shooting hand.

The injury is to Gray's ring finger and pinkie. Per Atlanta sports anchor Alison Mastrangelo of WSBTV, Gray had a minor procedure on the injury.

Gray didn't clarify to Mastrangelo what the procedure was, and the Dream haven't clarified the precise nature of the injury. Gray told Mastrangelo that she's considered day-to-day.

Gray initially suffered the injury in the first quarter of Game 1 of Atlanta's semifinal matchup against the New York Liberty on Oct. 4.

She returned to the court in the second quarter with tape around her fingers that she removed after play resumed. She took contact on her hand again and left the game for good before halftime.

The Dream ruled her out a day ahead of time for Game 2 of the series and initially listed her as day-to-day before she was also sidelined for Game 3.

Despite Gray's injury, the Dream swept the Liberty in three games to earn their place in the WNBA Finals.

Gray is a four-time All-Star, a standout two-way player and Atlanta's leading scorer. During the regular season, she averaged a career-high 19 points alongside 3.5 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.4 steals per game while shooting 46.2% from the floor and 33.8% from 3.

The Finals appearance is the first for Atlanta since 2013. They've played in the Finals three times, but are seeking the franchise's first WNBA championship. The Valkyries are making their first Finals appearance in their second season of existence.

articles.title: Payton Pritchard, Celtics Agree to Contract Extension, Full Details and NBA Salary Cap Impact
articles.summary: Payton Pritchard is reportedly staying with the only NBA team he has ever known for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
Payton Pritchard is reportedly staying with the only NBA team he has ever known for the foreseeable future.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday the guard and the Boston Celtics agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension that also features a mutual option in the 2029-30 campaign.

According to Spotrac , the Celtics have just under $28 million in total cap allocations for the upcoming 2026-27 season and $232.3 million in total cap allocations for the 2027-28 campaign.

Boston selected Pritchard with the No. 26 overall pick of the 2020 NBA draft, and he has developed into a franchise building block

After helping lead the Celtics to the championship during the 2023-24 campaign, he won the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year during the 2024-25 season while averaging 14.3 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game while connecting on 40.7 percent of his three-point attempts.

That shooting has been particularly important in Pritchard's career, as it has allowed him to fully capitalize on the additional space that comes when opposing defenses focus on other stars such as Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.

But he was far more than just a secondary playmaker for the Celtics last season with Tatum sidelined for an extended stretch. He averaged career-best numbers with 17.0 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds per game during 79 appearances and 50 starts.

Pritchard figures to play an important role in Boston again in 2026-27 with Brown no longer on the team after he was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers. It will be up to the guard to make opponents pay for collapsing on Tatum and Paul George, and he has proven the ability to do that throughout his career.

At just 28 years old, the Oregon product should remain a key piece in the backcourt throughout the entirety of the extension.

With the new contract in place, he and the Celtics will start the season on Oct. 20 against the Detroit Pistons.

articles.title: Celtics reportedly sign G Payton Pritchard to 2-year, $44.2 million extension, with a mutual option
articles.summary: Pritchard was in the second year of his 4-year rookie extension signed ahead of the 2024-2025 season.
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics are reportedly signing guard Payton Pritchard to a two-year, $44.2 million extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal also includes a mutual option for the 2029-2030 season, and it is fully guaranteed.

The Celtics selected Pritchard with the 26th overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. He helped them win the 2024 NBA championship and was named the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year in 2025.

The Boston guard has been used off the bench throughout his career, but he started 50 games last year, a significant increase from three the year before. Pritchard averaged a career-high 17 points per game last year. He also averaged 3.9 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 32.4 minutes per game.

Pritchard is once again projected to come off the bench this season. Derrick White is expected to start at point guard, with Baylor Scheierman at shooting guard. The Celtics will likely rely more on Pritchard off the bench this season, because former guard Jaylen Brown now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers.

Despite being a first-round pick, the guard has carved out a role as a depth player. He tended to fly under the radar, but had his first breakout game on April 9, 2023, against the Atlanta Hawks.

Pritchard finished with 30 points and hit nine 3-pointers. He added 14 rebounds and 11 assists for his first triple-double.

The guard's best scoring output came on March 5, 2025, when he drilled 10 3-pointers and finished with 43 points. Pritchard also grabbed 10 rebounds.

He has 16 games in which he has made at least five 3-pointers. Pritchard is shooting 39.4% from beyond the arc in his career. Last year, he averaged 7.1 3-point attempts per game, the 18th most in the league.

The Boston guard's 37.7% 3-point percentage ranked 11th-highest among players who attempted that many shots from beyond the arc.

Pritchard and the Celtics will open the 2026-2027 NBA season on Oct. 20 on the road against the Detroit Pistons.

articles.title: Justin Robinson da el triunfo al Barça con un triple salvador
articles.standfirst: Tercera victoria europea del curso para los azulgrana ante un Maccabi que peleó hasta el final con un gran Madar
articles.summary: Tercera victoria europea del curso para los azulgrana ante un Maccabi que peleó hasta el final con un gran Madar
articles.body: Un triple del base Justin Robins a 1.6 segundos del final dio la victoria al Barça este martes en el Palau Blaugrana (90-87) frente al Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv, en un encuentro igualado que los azulgranas dominaron con mínimas ventajas durante la mayor parte del tiempo. El escolta Kevin Punter (19 puntos), secundado por el base Umoja Gibson (13) y el alero Joel Parra (11), lideró en ataque el conjunto azulgrana, que pudo romper el partido en múltiples ocasiones, pero estuvo muy irregular en el tiro y la defensa, algo que aprovechó especialmente el base Yan Madar, que fue el mejor de los visitantes con 22 puntos. Contagiados por el frío ambiente del Palau Blaugrana, más vacío de lo habitual por la coincidencia con el partido de la 'Champions' de fútbol entre el Galatasaray y el Barcelona, ambos equipos empezaron tibios en defensa, lo que derivó en un tanteo alto (14-11, min.5), impulsado el Barça por Punter y Robinson, y entregado el Maccabi al tiro exterior. Las rotaciones, en espacial la entrada de Theis y Colson, dotaron de pegada interior y músculo al equipo israelí, que atrancó el ataque azulgrana, muy fluido hasta entonces. Con dificultades para mover la bola y encontrar ventajas en estático, el cuadro de Sekulic terminó el primer asalto en desventaja (23-24). La igualdad imperó en un segundo cuarto de poca continuidad en el juego y muchas imprecisiones (31-33, min.15). El Barça igualó el listón físico, mitigó la sangría en el rebote y pudo correr en varias ocasiones, pero le faltó puntería en tiros fáciles para reflejar en el marcador su leve mejoría en el juego. Estos errores, además, parecieron minar por momentos la confianza del equipo, que desatendió el perímetro y facilitó el gran acierto exterior del Maccabi (9 de 18 en la primera parte), que se marchó al descanso por delante en el marcador (40-42). Ajustó la mirilla el Barça tras el paso por vestuarios, con un rápido parcial de 8-0, pero Madar, defendido con una permisividad excesiva, abortó la escapada local con 10 puntos consecutivos (55-54, min.25) y devolvió la igualdad al juego, sin que ninguno de los dos equipos lograra anotar con continuidad o imponer su juego. Así, se llegó con un resultado ajustado (67-64) al último cuarto. El Barça amenazó con romper el partido en varias ocasiones, mediante Punter (74-68, min.33) y Gibson (83-75, min.35), pero después de los tiempos del Maccabi, los azulgranas cometían pérdidas o descuidos en defensa que permitían al cuadro israelí reengancharse al partido. El conjunto azulgrana llegó a los dos minutos finales con cinco puntos de ventaja pero tanto Punter como Robinson fallaron en sendos aclarados y el Maccabi, a base de tiros libres, se acercó a un punto a falta de 50 segundos. Punter amplió a tres la renta desde la línea de personal, pero Lundberg, en una falta muy protestada por el Barça al entender que había dejado la pierna al lanzar para ser golpeado por Parra, empató a 19.2 del final. La última bola fue para Robinson, que encestó el triple ganador a falta de 1.6, y Colson estrelló el último tiro del partido contra el tablero (90-87). De este modo, el equipo de Sekulic logró la tercera victoria europea del curso en cinco jornadas. 90. articles.title: Why Heat have by far the worst 2026-27 NBA Cup court
articles.summary: NBA Cup Court designs are often polarizing. Every team wears vibrant, unique jerseys during in-season tournament games that are both meant to be standoutish...
articles.body:
NBA Cup Court designs are often polarizing. Every team wears vibrant, unique jerseys during in-season tournament games that are both meant to be standoutish and represent the city of the team donning them. The courts are supposed to match. However, some NBA Cup courts have historically been a nightmare.

They can distract from gameplay or just look plain ugly. This year, while NBA Cup court designs were notably more simple than normal, the Miami Heat stood out as having the worst design for their playing surface. So, why did Miami miss the mark?

In the past, everyone has looked forward to what crazy designs and colors the Heat would rock on NBA Cup games or with their alternate uniforms. The team's famous blue, pink, and black "Vice City" jerseys, for example, are some of the most beloved threads in NBA history. Just last year, the Heat ranked as having the fourth best City Edition jerseys.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Of course, not everyone will like such an in-your-face design, but the splashy history fits the city of Miami well. In 2026-27, though, the Heat somehow have arguably the most boring and bland NBA Cup court design. For starters, the yellow base color looks more like your standard hardwood than anything that is supposed to draw fan's eyes.

Plus, it is hard to make out the NBA Cup trophies at center court and in the lanes because of the base color. Furthermore, the out-of-bounds areas are a simple plain black. Other teams used bold color choices, or, at the bare minimum, patterns and designs on the baseline/sideline out-of-bounds. The Heat went with nothingness.

Everything about this NBA Cup court feels bland, and that is only enhanced by the Heat's vibrant history. Miami has the worst courts in the league.

articles.title: Los tres 'pequeños' hacen grande al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Maledon (16+3+4), Feliz (15+5+5) y Campazzo (13+4+6) hacen un traje al Armani
articles.summary: Maledon (16+3+4), Feliz (15+5+5) y Campazzo (13+4+6) hacen un traje al Armani
articles.body: El Real Madrid rompió dos maldiciones de una tacada, interrelacionadas ambas, con su justa y trabajada victoria en Milán (89-98). Fue su primer triunfo a domicilio en esta Euroliga tras haber encadenado tres derrotas fuera (Dubai, Efes y Hapoel) y rompió el maleficio que le perseguía en cancha del Armani, donde había caído las tres últimas temporadas, maldición conjurada por la magia que desplegaron sus tres pequeños manejadores. Maledon (16+3+4), Feliz (15+5+5) y Campazzo (13+4+6) sublimaron el arte del baloncesto y demostraron que en un deporte de altos donde la estatura es fundamental, la inteligencia y la sapiencia a la hora de administrar los recursos de un equipo lo son aún más. Esos tres bajitos hicieron un traje a un Armani, al que borraron del mapa comandando un parcial de 3-24 del minuto 18 al 22 (42-63). Bolmaro (21+3+5) y las muñecas de Hall (17) y Mathews (14) evitaron una sangría mayor para el colista. Los italianos llevaron la iniciativa al ritmo de la muñeca de un enchufado Devon Hall, que aprovechó la laxitud defensiva blanca para demostrar su infalible puntería. El Madrid lo contrarrestó haciendo llegar el balón a Tavares, un seguro de vida bajo el aro. Pedro Martínez introdujo cinco cambios casi de golpe para meter una marcha más. Los triples de Okeke y Jones pusieron el contrapunto a los de Hall y Burnell mientras Campazzo se adueñaba del ritmo... hasta que su técnico lo cambió. El Armani dio otro zarpazo con los triples de Bolmaro y Mathews antes del final del primero cuarto (25-21, min10). Para entonces el Madrid ya había hecho 10 cambios. Maledon tomó el mando del partido al inicio del segundo acto dirigiendo con maestría y anotando con fluidez para comandar el sorpasso madridista (28-32, min 13). Martínez sentó al base francés en su mejor momento... pero le salió bien el incomprensible movimiento al técnico porque entró Campazzo para exhibir su mejor versión de la temporada. El base argentino movió a la defensa milanista a su antojo, anotó dos triples y asistió a Jones, y Abalde para que anotasen otros dos. Los blancos encontraron por fin su inspiración desde el triple (8/12) y el Facu comandó con su magia un descomunal parcial de 3-24 entre el final de la primera parte y el inicio del segundo, ya con Maledon, otro de sus magos, en cancha (42-63, min 23). Pedro Martínez fue fiel a su filosofía y en la primera parte agitó la coctelera como si no hubiese un mañana, realizando hasta 21 cambios, que en la segunda 'sólo' fueron 18. Y esa frenética entrada y salida de personal le salió bien al entrenador barcelonés. Es posible que tanto vaivén volviese un poco locos a sus jugadores, pero a los que de verdad mareó fue a su homológo italiano, Pepe Poeta, y a los jugadores de este, que entraron en barrena. Cuando todo parecía perdido para los italianos, en la lona al final del tercer cuarto (67-84) tras otros 10 cambios de Pedro Martínez, apareció Bolmaro para echarse al equipo a su espalda, y a lomos del base argentino el Armani recuperó el aliento y soñó con la remontada tras un triple de Mathews y una técnica al banquillo blanco (72-84, min 32). Pero los tres pequeños del Madrid les despertaron adueñándose del partido y evitando que el equipo blanco entrase en pánico, y los milanistas tuvieron que conformarse con maquillar el marcador (89-98) y seguirán al menos dos días más como colistas de la Euroliga, mientras el Madrid remonta posiciones. 89 – Armani Olimpia Milán (25+15+27+22): Thompson (-), Hall (17), Guduric (8), Peters (1), Wright (11) -cinco inicial-; Cole (7), Burnell (3), Mathews (14), Bolmaro (21), Ricci (-), Booker (7). 98 – Real Madrid (21+32+31+14): Smith Jr. (2), Maledon (16), Procida (1), Jantunen (6), Tavares (10) -cinco inicial-, Feliz (15), Campazzo (13), Pradilla (8), Okeke (6), Luwawu-Cabarrot (3), Abalde (6) y Jones (12). Árbitros: Ilija Belosevic (Serbia), Tomasz Trawicki (Polonia) y Hugues Thepenier (Francia). Sin eliminados. articles.title: Valkyries' Joe Lacob Talks Role in Helping Dream Change Locations for WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries governor Joe Lacob revealed that he helped influence the decision to move the first two Atlanta Dream home games of the 2026 WNBA Finals from Gateway Center Arena to State Farm Arena.
articles.body:
Golden State Valkyries governor Joe Lacob revealed that he helped influence the decision to move the first two Atlanta Dream home games of the 2026 WNBA Finals from Gateway Center Arena to State Farm Arena.

"I put quite a bit of pressure on the commissioner of the NBA and the WNBA," Lacob told Janie McCauley of the Associated Press. "I felt, look, it's not really about us it's about the league. The look would not be too good to have Ballhalla and 18,000 fans here and 3,500 over there."

He explained that he wanted to crowd atmosphere to feel the same in Atlanta and Golden State ahead of their Finals matchup.

"I think it's important for the league to play these games in the Finals, a great championship between two very good teams, in front of the same kind of crowd in both places," Lacob said, per McCauley .

On Tuesday, the WNBA announced the venue change for Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta.

Gateway Center Arena, the usual home of the Dream, has the smallest capacity in the WNBA at just 3,500. Meanwhile, State Farm Arena can seat over 17,000 fans.

If the change wasn't made, there would have been a stark contrast in the crowd sizes for Atlanta and Golden State during the series. The Valkyries are set to host the first pair of games of the 2026 Finals at the Chase Center, which has a capacity of 18,064.

The Dream enter the series with plenty of momentum, as they swept the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty in the first two rounds of the playoffs.

The Valkyries also haven't faced much resistance, going 5-1 in the postseason while taking down the Dallas Wings and Las Vegas Aces.

Game 1 between Atlanta and Golden State is on Saturday, with tip-off at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Sinfonía incompleta del Valencia que cae en la prórroga ante el campeón
articles.standfirst: El Olympiacos remonta en 19 minutos una desventaja de 28 puntos
articles.summary: El Olympiacos remonta en 19 minutos una desventaja de 28 puntos
articles.body: Dijo Rudy Tomjanovich en 1995 "nunca subestimes el corazón de un campeón". Y esa frase debe servir para explicar en gran parte el partido del Roig Arena que ganó el Olympiacos en la prórroga, 97-102. El Valencia firmó una sinfonía que duró 21 minutos. Con un minuto de juego en el tercer cuarto ganaba por 28, 62-34, y desde ahí, se dejó toda su ventaja para dejar que el Olympiacos igualara primero y ganara después. La primera parte del Valencia fue sublime, un deleite baloncestístico. Son 20 minutos que se pueden ver en bucle para disfrutar de la esencia de este deporte. Ya forman parte de la historia más bella del Valencia. Los de Xavi Albert desarbolaron al campeón de Europa. Desde el inicio, con un 10-0 que sorprendió a los griegos con una ventaja que no dejó de crecer: 31-17 al final del primer cuarto y 59-34 al descanso. Ni los 26 cambios que hizo Albert en esos 20 minutos influyeron en el ritmo, todo lo contrario, lo alimentaron. Era el Valencia en estado puro. Con un minuto de juego del tercer acto, triple de Brooks y máxima taronja que estaba aplastando a su rival. Pero el rival es el actual campeón de Europa y resulta que ha presentado sus credenciales para repetir. Milutinov se adueñó del partido y lideró la remontada griega. Todo lo bueno que hizo, lo firmó tras el descanso. El Olympiacos ni siquiera notó la expulsión de su entrenador, Bartzokas, por dos técnicas. Al contrario, se motivaron: Fournier acudió al rescate y Papanikolaou ayudó. pero por encima de todos estuvo Montero. El pabellón que le vio brillar tantas veces, lo volvió a ver, pero esta vez para golpear al Valencia con 26 puntos y jugadas clave cuando se acercaba el final. El dominicano no sólo se ha adaptado al juego del Olympiacos, ha hecho el equipo suyo. Es más valioso en pista que Vezenkov, y ya es decir. Con 88-90 (Fournier y Montero fallaron un tiro libre cada uno), Shorts obra un milagro con un canastón a aro pasado para enviar el partido a la prórroga. El tiempo extra tuvo toda la tensión del mundo, pero poco acierto, sobre todo del Valencia que falló todos sus tiros de campo (seis) para anotar sólo desde el libre. El Oly, que ganó la segunda parte 31-56, se llevó el triunfo en una prórroga que supo encarar mejor, demostrando el corazón de campeón que late en una fabulosa plantilla. Y dejó al Valencia con una sinfonía incompleta.

articles.title: Pablo Torre 'Looking Into' LeBron James' Helicopter Contract after Joining 76ers
articles.summary: Journalist and podcaster Pablo Torre says he is "looking into" a contract between Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James and Fanatics that reportedly includes on-demand helicopter travel.
articles.body:
Journalist and podcaster Pablo Torre says he is "looking into" a contract between Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James and Fanatics that reportedly includes on-demand helicopter travel.

ESPN's Dave McMenamin previously reported James was using a helicopter to commute while splitting his time between New York and Philadelphia after signing with the Sixers this offseason.

Front Office Sports' Daniel Roberts and TMZ Sports added last week the travel was taking place in a Fanatics-branded helicopter as part of James' endorsement deal with the company.

Torre told Roberts he considered the story to be "something of interest to the league" in a Tuesday episode of Front Office Sports' Tuned In.

"We're also getting tips from NBA owners, who are sending me your story, being like, 'What is this?'" Torre told Roberts.

TMZ reported James' "use of any Fanatics aircraft is part of his 'broad long term deal' with the company."

Similar charter flights to the ones James is taking between New York and Philadelphia cost around $6,000 to $9,000 each way, according to TMZ.

Roberts reported the endorsement deal between Fanatics and James "extends to after his playing career is over."

According to Roberts, "a small handful of other athletes with big Fanatics deals get same access" to the brand's aviation.

The staff of Pablo Torre Finds Out won a Pulitzer Prize in Audio Reporting this May for their investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the Los Angeles Clippers, which were penalized in September by the NBA.

James signed a two-year, $8 million deal with a second-year player option earlier this summer before making his debut for the Sixers in preseason action last Thursday against the Brooklyn Nets.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer is set to tip off his first regular season with the Sixers next Tuesday in a road game against the defending champion New York Knicks.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "No tenemos previsto acudir al mercado por la lesión de Deck"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Real Madrid confirma que no ficharán para sustituir al argentino
articles.summary: El técnico del Real Madrid confirma que no ficharán para sustituir al argentino
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, afirmó que no está previsto que el club acuda al mercado después de conocerse la lesión de larga duración de alero internacional argentino Gabriel 'Gaby' Deck, quien debe pasar por el quirófano y estará varios meses de baja por una inestabilidad anterior en el hombro izquierdo, tras un episodio de luxación articular. "No está previsto. Tenemos una plantilla muy larga. Ahora mismo tenemos dos lesionados de larga duración, pero consideramos que podemos seguir siendo competitivos con los jugadores que tenemos, como lo hemos demostrado hoy", señaló en la rueda de prensa posterior al duelo de la Euroliga en el que su equipo se impuso a domicilio al Armani Olimpia Milán por 89-98. Martínez afirmó que lo que más le gusto del partido fue "la capacidad de sobreponernos a unos primeros minutos con demasiadas pérdidas" y destacó los buenos minutos que jugaron en el tercer cuarto: "Creo que ha sido nuestro mejor momento en lo que va de temporada. En ese tramo anotamos varios tiros libres, metimos dos buenos tiros... y el baloncesto es un deporte muy emocional, así que cuando anotas, tal vez defiendes todavía mejor". En cuanto a los nombres propios, restó importancia al hecho de que Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot no brillara en esta ocasión: "Jugamos muchos partidos, algunas semanas tres o cuatro. A todos nos gustaría que los jugadores estuvieran siempre bien, pero esto es un juego de equipo. Unos días destacan unos y otros, otros. No estoy preocupado porque alguno no haya tenido hoy su mejor día, porque todos son de tremenda calidad y van a tener todos oportunidades para resarcirse de alguna mala actuación". También habló acerca de Nick Smith Jr.: "Cada partido es diferente. Jugamos hace dos días el último partido y tuvo una gran actuación, anotó fácil. Es un chico muy joven, es su primera experiencia fuera de su país y necesita tiempo para entender que aquí el baloncesto es un poco diferente. El ritmo, la defensa y el contacto físico son diferentes aquí y tiene que aprender, pero es otro chico con una excelente mentalidad". "No esperamos que sea una superestrella para nosotros; lo que esperamos de él y de los demás es que ayude al equipo de diferentes maneras, unos días más y otros días menos, pero siempre con la misma mentalidad de intentar ayudar al equipo en defensa, en el rebote... y suele hacerlo muy bien", completó.

articles.title: El Valencia rumia su derrota más dura: "No sé si ha sido miedo, pero debemos seguir siendo valientes"
articles.standfirst: Xavi Albert, técnico taronja, pide a sus jugadores que aprendan la lección después de caer ante Olympiacos tras ir ganando por 28 puntos
articles.summary: Xavi Albert, técnico taronja, pide a sus jugadores que aprendan la lección después de caer ante Olympiacos tras ir ganando por 28 puntos
articles.body: El entrenador del Valencia Basket, Xavi Albert, lamentó tras caer su equipo en la prórroga ante el Olympiacos que en un momento determinado del partido pensaran en gestionar una ventaja que fue de casi treinta puntos y pidió a los suyos que aprendan la lección y sean valientes. "Ha sido una derrota dura, ha habido una parte para cada equipo. La primera hemos mostrado una identidad muy clara y hemos dominado pero en la segunda no podemos pensar en controlar la distancia, se ve cada día que se pueden recuperar distancias más grandes", apuntó en una rueda de prensa. "No podemos pensar en proteger un marcador porque lo hemos generado. Ha habido un momento que no sé si ha sido miedo pero tenemos que seguir jugando valientes, no tenemos que gestionar el marcador, porque cada vez se recuperan más parciales", añadió. El técnico afirmó que, más allá de que la defensa de cambios del Olympiacos de la segunda parte, fue su cambio de mentalidad el que marcó el choque pero recordó que hace dos semanas la situación se dio al revés cuando ganaron en la pista del ASVEL. "Los partidos son muy largos", subrayó. Albert dijo que espera que el equipo debe aprender de esta derrota, que la mentalidad no debe ser "negociable" y que deben tratar de ser mejor equipo de lo que ahora son. "El Olympiacos dio un gran paso adelante físico, jugaron de otra manera y nos sacaron del ritmo", explicó. Por su parte, Christos Papas, segundo técnico del Olympiacos, felicitó al Valencia por el esfuerzo en el partido y por el equipo que ha montado. El ayudante de Georgios Bartzokas dijo que formaron una primera parte "desastrosa" pero que en la segunda "cambiaron" el momento del partido desde la defensa por lo que felicitó a sus jugadores y dijo que piensan ya en el Barcelona.

articles.summary: As LSU continues to buck college sports norms, the school hands the reins of its men’s basketball team to Will Wade, who appears hellbent on doing things his own way.
articles.body: Dense fog rolled into Baton Rouge on Tuesday morning, bad enough to earn an advisory from the Weather Channel, and thick enough to do the one thing no one else in college athletics seemingly can do: Stop LSU. The Tigers’ entourage, scheduled to appear here for SEC Basketball Media Day, could not take off due to the fog, grounding them for their session, the league announced. Who says Mother Nature doesn’t have a sense of humor? A program shrouded in controversy, willing to bring all the smoke and run around like college sports’ Pigpen (of Peanuts fame), gets stuck in Baton Rouge because of fog. “Next year maybe we’ll all have a little fog, right?” one coach said with a chuckle. One month after football coach Lane Kiffin fought to suit up two would-be NFL players in a college game, LSU men’s basketball coach Will Wade is attempting to build a roster with two players who went through the NBA Draft process, two others who have played professionally overseas and two who are part of court orders seeking eligibility for fifth-year college players (Donovan Dent has been granted an injunction; Skyy Clark has not). The man who, in his first iteration at LSU got fired for making “strong-ass” offers against NCAA rules, now says he is simply being “unconventional” in his attempt to flout loopholes and lean into injunctions. Wade’s unconventional attempt at roster building is, in order, against SEC rules, against NCAA rules and contingent on courts ordering against the NCAA, which is currently 3-0 in appeals. The upshot: Three weeks before its first real game, LSU has 10 players listed on its webpage. Along with Dent, whose status could change on appeal, one is the son of his assistant coach, and another is a 5-foot-10-inch, 150-pound freshman. “We’ll have a few more guys eligible for our next exhibition game tomorrow,” Wade said on the SEC Network via Zoom. “And we anticipate building this thing as we head toward November 13.” There is no evidence that that will, in fact, happen. Pressed by a reporter on a Zoom call about specific players, Wade grew agitated and defiant. But in his tirade of a response, he also said some truths. One: RJ Luis “is not rostered.” Luis, the one-time Big East Player of the Year who signed multiple NBA contracts, won a court injunction in August allowing him to play, but Wade said the school was “following SEC protocols,” which includes prohibiting players who have signed pro deals to compete. Two: Marcio Santos is officially gone, having left LSU to sign a pro deal in Spain. To be clear, LSU is not alone. Back in the day, coaches hit the courts in Las Vegas and at Peach Jam, the summer recruiting locales, to find players. Now, they await word from the actual courts. As coaches took the podium here, a judge in Colorado was hearing an NCAA appeal about the eligibility of thousands of would-be fifth years. Missouri coach Dennis Gates moved up his appearance here by a day so he could join Mark Mitchell, who signed what’s called an NBA Exhibit 10 contract, at a hearing on Wednesday to determine if he could play. Tennessee’s Jalen Washington remains ineligible after the NCAA won a stay on a temporary injunction that would have allowed the Vanderbilt transfer to play. Meanwhile, Oklahoma coach Porter Moser opened his remarks by saying he was excited to talk “retention,” but admitted that to keep players he had to “shrink the gap.” In other words, scrounge up more money. With its small numbers, college basketball is especially susceptible to the high risk/high reward world of current roster construction. But Wade is not assuming risk; he is all in. Whereas Kiffin was trying to clear two guys on roster of 105, he is rolling the dice on what will be the difference between fielding an actual SEC team or a glorified CYO program. And he is doing it after the SEC threatened everything up to, and including, expulsion if Kiffin didn’t back down. Already poked, the league bear hasn’t exactly gone into hibernation, either. The SEC’s lawsuit is still out there, the league due to file a response to LSU’s motion to dismiss on Tuesday, and one of the players Wade is trying to clear, Saliou Niang, was drafted 58th by the Cavaliers. Though he didn’t sign a pro contract, the SEC policy says that any athlete who has “previously declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA and did not properly withdraw” cannot compete. But LSU is as all-in as its coach. As with Kiffin, when the governor shoved former athletic director Scott Woodward out the door when he balked at hiring the coveted coach and all of his baggage, LSU has greased the skids for Wade. He is surrounded by people who gave him his initial cleanse. A year after LSU fired Wade amid an NCAA investigation that included five Level I violations, McNeese State hired him, doubling down on his renegade reputation. In a marketing campaign, Wade donned a black cowboy hat. The university president who OK’d the hire at McNeese – Wade Rousse — is now the president at LSU. A wealthy construction company owner who befriended Wade while he was in Lake Charles, Lee Mallett, is now LSU’s chairman of the board, and Wade’s former athletic director, Heath Schroyer, is now not just a senior associate AD for the Tigers. Wade’s contract specifies that he reports directly to Schroyer, and not AD Verge Ausberry. These are his people, and if they don’t necessarily endorse the renegade, they don’t mind Will being Will. At a local rotary club meaning, he joked about joining Kiffin on staff, saying he’s no longer the most controversial coach on campus, and zinged his own checkered pass. “Everyone says it’s ‘name, image and likeness,’” he said of NIL. “I say, it’s ‘now it’s legal.’” Nor has he backed down on the risk he’s taking, arguing that it will beat the 3-15 league finish from a year ago. “So I mean, hell, what’s the downside?” he said earlier this year. “We’re giving ourselves a chance at incredible upside, and if we’re no good, all right, we just have to live through one more bad year. We’ve had a few of them.” This is about nothing more – or less – than winning. Five years ago, LSU brought Kim Mulkey in to resuscitate its women’s basketball program, ignoring the controversy that trailed her like a train of sequins off one of her gaudy pantsuits. Two years later, she won them a national title. The football team hasn’t won a national title since 2019. LSU opened the season ranked 11th. The basketball team has never won it all, but Wade turned the Tigers relevant for the first time since Shaq and Dale Brown. In five seasons, he went to three NCAA Tournaments and won the SEC regular-season title in 2019. To make a fire, you need some smoke. Or at least a little fog.

articles.title: Angel Reese Praised by Valkyries HC, 'Huge Reason' Dream Advanced to WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase has been impressed with Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese as the two teams prepare to face off in the 2026 WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase has been impressed with Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese as the two teams prepare to face off in the 2026 WNBA Finals.

"She's the ultimate, ultra competitor to me," Nakase told reporters Tuesday. "When we were at USA, you heard her voice constantly. So when she didn't start, you heard her. She was constantly cheering her teammates on when they needed to, she constantly called them out when we needed energy. So, understanding she's a huge reason why I think that team is in the Finals, Atlanta, because she brings this competitive edge and she's not gonna let any possession slip."

Nakase has some familiarity with Reese, as she served as an assistant coach for the United States during the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. Reese operated as a key rotation piece for a U.S. squad that won gold in the event, averaging a team-high 2.5 offensive rebounds per game.

The 24-year-old has put together an impressive 2026 season for the Dream, taking home Defensive Player of the Year honors while also earning her third consecutive All-Star nod.

Reese has remained impactful in the playoffs, averaging 18.0 points and 8.4 rebounds to go along with 2.2 blocks per game across five contests. She's shooting 43.3 percent from the field and 38.5 percent from three-point territory in the postseason.

The Dream own a plus-17.5 net rating with Reese on the floor in the playoffs, which drops to a minus-11.6 net rating with her on the bench (via WNBA.com ).

Game 1 between Atlanta and Golden State is on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NBA announcer Mike Tirico addresses the truth behind Michael Jordan's, limited NBC role
articles.summary: Mike Tirico defends NBC Sports' Michael Jordan interview, saying people are still talking about it a year later despite criticism of the segments.
articles.body: NBC’s return to NBA coverage last season offered longtime basketball fans a dose of nostalgia. The venerable broadcast network regained the league’s rights as part of an 11-year media deal, reviving the iconic theme song that accompanied NBA broadcasts from 1990 to 2002. Disney-owned ESPN and Amazon Prime Video also joined the deal, which marked the NBA’s move away from longtime broadcast partner TNT. As NBC prepared to launch its 2025-26 NBA coverage, the network announced that former Chicago Bulls superstar and six-time NBA champion Michael Jordan had been named a "special contributor." Some interpreted the announcement as a signal that Jordan would become a regular presence on the studio desk. Instead, his role amounted to a single sit-down interview with lead play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico, which NBC split into several segments and aired throughout the season. MICHAEL WILBON REVEALS JORDAN'S TRUE FEELINGS ABOUT LEBRON MIKE BREEN SAYS FANS 'DESERVE TO BE THROWN A BONE' AS NBA CUTS ALL LOCAL BROADCASTS FROM THE PLAYOFFS Jordan is not expected to reprise his role when the 2026-27 NBA season tips off next Tuesday. Nearly a year after NBC’s announcement, questions about Jordan's limited involvement continue to linger. Tirico argued that continued interest in the interview validated NBC’s decision to let Jordan’s limited role speak for itself. "I love the fact that we did one interview —and you can say what you want about it airing once or being spread out over our series of pregame shows during the year— it’s a year later and people are still talking about it," Tirico said Tuesday in New York City during an onstage interview at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit. "And people are still asking about it. Which, to me, is all the reason that it was completely worth it." Instead of addressing the NBA’s daily headlines or weighing in on current players, Jordan’s interview focused on broader topics, including load management and his enduring love for basketball. That approach may have disappointed viewers hoping to hear the basketball icon discuss players such as LeBron James or major storylines such as the controversy involving Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers. Tirico, however, maintains that the segments provided an authentic view of Jordan’s personality. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I think Michael Jordan hadn’t been on TV for a long time for a reason," Tirico said. "He likes being Michael Jordan. Even still, when he’s on camera, there’s an aura about Michael Jordan that is just different. Sitting across from him. It’s just a different feel. I think he is above the daily discourse of, ‘Hey, who is the best point guard in the NBA right now?’ and ‘who’s the best this or the best that?’" If another sit-down can be arranged in the future, Tirico would eagerly welcome Jordan back, regardless of the subject matter. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD "I will say that it was damn cool to hang with MJ and talk basketball, and talk business and golf and all that other stuff," Tirico said. "If he wanted to be— we would all run to have him on every single day. But that’s just not what he wants to do, I think, at this point in his career and life." The defending champion New York Knicks then host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers, while the Western Conference champion San Antonio Spurs close the night against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

articles.title: Fixer in Lucrative NCAA Basketball Betting Scheme Sentenced to 6 years in Prison
articles.summary: A man charged with rigging college basketball games as part of an elaborate point-fixing scheme that raked in millions was sentenced to six years in federal prison, prosecutors in Pennsylvania announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
A man charged with rigging college basketball games as part of an elaborate point-fixing scheme that raked in millions was sentenced to six years in federal prison, prosecutors in Pennsylvania announced on Tuesday.

It was the first penalty handed down as part of an investigation that revealed a sprawling network of professional gamblers and college basketball players who, prosecutors say, profited off fixed games.

Prosecutors said Jalen Smith, 30, played a "central role" in helping fix games in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 NCAA Division I basketball seasons, placing bets and recruiting players with the promise of a big payment for purposefully underperforming during a game, U.S. Attorney David Metcalf said on Tuesday. Bettors would then wager against the players' teams in those games, defrauding sportsbooks and other gamblers, authorities said. Smith pleaded guilty earlier this year to bribery and wire fraud charges.

The sentencing comes at the start of the 2026-27 NCAA basketball season, when bettors will wager billions of dollars both legally and illegally on games nationwide. In the meantime, law enforcement, regulators and sports leagues have struggled to keep up with gambling's growing popularity in collegiate and professional sports alike.

"Today's sentencing sends a clear message: Those who exploit professional and collegiate athletes for personal gain will be held accountable," said Wayne A. Jacobs, special agent in charge of the FBI's Philadelphia office. "This conduct does more than harm individual athletes. It undermines the integrity of sports and the trust placed in fair competition."

The point-shaving scheme Smith was involved in is said to have involved nearly 30 NCAA basketball games, and included schools like DePaul University, State University of New York at Buffalo and Tulane University, among others.

Prosecutors accused Smith and at least 26 other named defendants of wagering millions of dollars and paying hundreds of thousands of dollars to players in bribes. Payments to players typically ranged from $10,000 to $30,000 per game, according to an indictment.

Smith and others strategically targeted players considered "underdogs" in games, encouraging them to underperform in order to guarantee certain spreads. Those players were prime targets, prosecutors said, because they were offered money that exceeded potential income from legitimate sponsorships.

Smith, of Charlotte, North Carolina, trained and developed local basketball players for professional scouting combines and used those connections with players when he became part of the scheme, according to prosecutors.

The point-shaving scheme resulted in more than $3 million in fraudulent wagers. Smith, who also pleaded guilty to a separate felony gun possession charge, will have to pay $1.1 million in restitution, which prosecutors said is the cost incurred by gambling platforms as a result of the scheme.

Besides the fixers who recruited players and placed bets, the charges targeted over a dozen former college basketball players and four other players who were active with their college teams last season.

articles.title: Red Wings Reportedly Closing In on Massive Alex DeBrincat Extension
articles.summary: Elliotte Friedman reports the Detroit Red Wings are nearing a massive seven-year, $91 million contract extension with Alex DeBrincat.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings may have finally received some good news following Tuesday night's heartbreaking 5-4 overtime loss to the New Jersey Devils. According to NHL insider Elliotte Friedman, Detroit is reportedly closing in on a massive contract extension with star forward Alex DeBrincat .

In a social media post attributed to Friedman on X , the NHL insider indicated that the Red Wings and DeBrincat are nearing an agreement on a seven-year contract worth approximately $13 million annually.

If finalized at those figures, the agreement would be worth approximately $91 million over seven seasons, making it one of the most significant financial commitments in franchise history.

Alex DeBrincat Extension Would Be Huge for Detroit

DeBrincat, a Farmington Hills native, is entering the final season of his four-year, $31.5 million contract with Detroit. Coming off a 41-goal, 85-point campaign in 2025-26, the 28-year-old was positioned for a substantial raise as he approached unrestricted free agency.

Earlier this month, NHL insider David Pagnotta indicated that DeBrincat was seeking between $12 million and $14 million annually , depending on the length of the agreement. The reported $13 million figure would fall directly within that range.

For a Red Wings organization dealing with uncertainty surrounding Dylan Larkin, Simon Edvinsson, and the direction of the franchise, securing DeBrincat would represent a significant commitment to keeping an established goal scorer in Detroit.

Oct 6, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings right wing Alex DeBrincat (93) passes the puck during the first period against the Ottawa Senators at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The potential extension would also create important financial implications for Detroit moving forward. At $13 million annually, DeBrincat would become one of the team's highest-paid players, placing additional pressure on management to construct a competitive roster around its expensive core.

However, allowing a three-time 40-goal scorer to reach free agency would carry its own risks, particularly for a franchise that has struggled to return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs. Locking up DeBrincat would give Detroit long-term stability on the wing and prevent another major contract situation from becoming an ongoing distraction.

The Red Wings have experienced a frustrating start to the 2026-27 season, but a potential $91 million agreement with Alex DeBrincat would provide some much-needed optimism. While no contract has been officially announced, the reported progress suggests Detroit is attempting to secure one of its most important offensive players for the foreseeable future.

articles.title: Angel Reese Reacts to Dream Hosting WNBA Finals Games at Hawks' Arena Ahead of Game 1 vs. Valkyries
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese says it will be "bittersweet" to move to a larger arena for at least two games of the 2026 WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese says it will be "bittersweet" to move to a larger arena for at least two games of the 2026 WNBA Finals.

The WNBA announced Tuesday the Dream would play Games 3 and 4 of the Finals at the team's future home of State Farm Arena, which seats more than 17,000, as opposed to the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena.

"I do love Gateway, so much, and I love the intimacy of being here and all the fans coming out and supporting us," Reese told WBS-TV Tuesday (0:49 mark of the video below. "And even if we couldn't go to State Farm, I was going to be grateful to just be able to be here and just have everybody here. We probably would've had a big TV outside, and everybody outside. It would be a whole cookout."

"But I am looking forward to everybody showing up and supporting us at State Farm, because every game has been a great turnout. Celebrities on the side... you don't know who you're going to see in Atlanta."

The Dream has played at Gateway Center Arena since 2021. The franchise announced last week the team would make a full-time move to State Farm Arena ahead of the 2027 season.

The move came after the Dream saw more than 400 percent growth in season ticket membership over the past five years, according to the team .

After the Dream clinched a Finals berth last Friday with a semifinal sweep of the New York Liberty, the WNBA shifted the schedule of the championship in order to accommodate playing Games 3 and 4 at the larger capacity venue.

It is not clear where Game 6 would take place, if necessary, because the current schedule conflicts with an Oct. 29 Atlanta Hawks game.

The Dream are preparing to battle for a title against the Golden State Valkyries, which have sold out every game at their own 18,000-person home of Chase Center for each of their two seasons in the WNBA.

Game 1 of the Finals is set to tip off Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET in San Francisco.

articles.title: “My mom never raised me to be that way”: LeBron James revisits his difficult childhood in Akron as he remains committed to helping the next generation
articles.summary: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, lived with his single mother in Akron, Ohio, before he was drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2004 and his life
articles.body: LeBron James, the 41 year old NBA icon, lived with his single mother in Akron, Ohio, before he was drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2004 and his life changed overnight. After playing in the league for over two decades, LeBron James reflects on the life he has had and how Akron inspired him to do better in life.LeBron James reflects on the life he lived in Akron before making it big in his life and how he still helps his hometownIn an interview with TIME Magazine, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon LeBron James opened up about his life as he said, “I had so much time to explore and imagine and want to be more than a little Black kid that stays in the house and feels sheltered…”The star player added, “When you feel like you are being slighted, that’s a motivating factor,” he says. “I felt slighted that I was in a single-parent household. I felt slighted because I didn’t have any siblings. So I’ve always felt a certain chip on my shoulder.”The four time NBA champion LeBron James continued, “If I would have listened to the narrative of the outside world, I would have been doomed…Because everybody said it was a bad idea. Why am I hiring people with no education? Why am I hiring people that haven’t been in the business? Why am I hiring my childhood friends?”LeBron James continued, “Everybody, when it comes to things that have never been done before, they want you to go to the sound of the beat that was from yesterday, or the beat that was from 10 years ago. My mom never raised me to be that way.”LeBron James has raised millions for Akron as he stands by the communities he belonged toOver the last two decades, LeBron James has often spoken about the issues he faced growing up in Akron and how he has been constantly looking for ways to improve things in his hometown.The first thing which LeBron James did after making it big in his career was set up the LeBron James Family Foundation.The charity has worked for the communities in Akron as he has even set up an education wing, the I PROMISE School which has established schools for his hometown’s children.In the last few months, LeBron James has also partnered with luxury brands, including Mercedes Maybach to help raise funds for the people of Akron.At a time when his move to the Philadelphia 76ers have sparked heated debates across the league, it seems all LeBron James is focusing on is getting back to the court and making it a successful season before he retires.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los Mavericks fichan a Jorge Díaz-Graham, el sexto español en la NBA y jugador número 1
articles.standfirst: Firma un contrato Exhibit 10 con Dallas y será el sexto español en la NBA junto a Sergio de Larrea, Santi Aldama, Aday Mara, Hugo González y Baba Miller
articles.summary: Firma un contrato Exhibit 10 con Dallas y será el sexto español en la NBA junto a Sergio de Larrea, Santi Aldama, Aday Mara, Hugo González y Baba Miller
articles.body: Jorge Díaz-Graham, ala-pívot canario de 23 años y 2,11 metros, se convierte en el tercer jugador de los Mavericks y en el sexto español de la NBA tras firmar un contrato Exhibit 10 con Dallas. El polivalente jugador español ha llegado a un acuerdo con los Mavs, en los que acompañará a Sergio de Larrea y Santi Aldama, una semana antes de que empiece la temporada NBA el 20 de octubre. Un contrato Exhibit 10 en la NBA es un vínculo laboral por una temporada, bajo el salario mínimo y sin dinero garantizado. Funciona como una cláusula de prueba de pretemporada. Una de sus principales características es que puede convertirse en un contrato two-way. Esta fórmula permitiría a Díaz-Graham alternar su participación entre los Mavericks de la NBA con su equipo afiliado en la G League, los Texas Legends. Otra opción es que Dallas corte al español, que podría incorporarse a los Legends y recibir una bonificación económica vinculada a su Exhibit 10 si permanece al menos 60 días en el vinculado de la G-League. Jorge Díaz-Graham convenció a los Mavericks con sus actuaciones en la Summer League de Las Vegas, en la que promedió 7,2 puntos, 5,4 rebotes y 1,8 asistencias. El multiusos español jugó en la cantera del La Laguna Tenerife hasta que dio el salto a Estados Unidos para jugar en MG Academy. En la NCAA jugó tres temporadas en Pittsburgh y un último curso en Oregon State. Con los 'Beavers' promedió 6 puntos, 3,6 rebotes y 1 asistencia en 17,9 minutos. Jorge Díaz Graham fue seleccionado con el número 1 por los Texas Legends en el Draft Internacional de la G-League, mientras que su hermano gemelo Guillermo Díaz Graham (San Francisco) fue seleccionado con el número 3 por el mismo equipo.

articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard's first game back with the Toronto Raptors—after what was a very eventful summer—went off without a hitch.

The star forward led the Raptors to a 148-98 win over the defending-champion New York Knicks in preseason action on Tuesday night, leading all scorers with 21 points.

Here's a look at Leonard's final box score:

Leonard looked good in the contest, showing his usual array of shot-making (and his penchant for securing some very lucky bounces in Toronto):

The Eastern Conference is loaded, no doubt, and playoff berths won't be easy to come by. But this Toronto team, at least on paper, looks like a potential contender.

articles.title: Aday Mara le demuestra a Shai que es su coloso impactando en los Thunder: mejor +/- y dobles dígitos
articles.standfirst: El pívot español volvió a firmar dobles dígitos en el primer triunfo de la pretemporada NBA de los Oklahoma City Thunder
articles.summary: El pívot español volvió a firmar dobles dígitos en el primer triunfo de la pretemporada NBA de los Oklahoma City Thunder
articles.body: Aday Mara, en su cuarto partido de la pretemporada de la NBA, demostró que tiene un hueco importante en la rotación de los Thunder en un partido en el que el técnico Mark Daigneault puso en liza a todas sus estrellas en el triunfo en la prórroga por 114-112 ante los Indiana Pacers en el Paycom Center de Oklahoma City. El pívot español, que oficialmente tiene una envergadura de 2,29 m. y un histórico alcance de 2,97 m., firmó dobles dígitos y fue el jugador con el mejor +/- (diferencia de puntos con él en pista) de los Thunder con +12 en el primer triunfo en la pretemporada de la franquicia de Oklahoma. Aday Mara salió desde el banquillo para firmar 10 puntos (4 de 5 en tiros de 2 y 2 de 2 tiros libres), 4 rebotes, 1 asistencia y 3 tapones en casi 19 minutos, en un partido en el que volvía a la rotación de Oklahoma el veterano Isaiah Hartenstein, pívot de 29 años y 2,13 m. que este verano renovó por 3 años y 75 millones de dólares. Hartenstein sumó 0 puntos (0 de 2 en tiros de 2 y 0 de 1 en triples), 1 rebote y 2 asistencias en 13 minutos saliendo como titular. En los Thunder, con todos los titulares en pista excepto Chet Holmgren a falta de una semana para que empiece la NBA, destacaron Jalen Williams (16 puntos), Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (15 puntos en 23 minutos) y Jared McCain (20 puntos con 6 de 12 en triples). Los mejores de los Indiana Pacers fueron Tyrese Haliburton (24 puntos y 4 de 6 en triples), Ivica Zubac (13 puntos y 13 rebotes) y Kelly Oubre Jr. (12 puntos). Haliburton volvía a Oklahoma City por primera vez desde su lesión del tendón de Aquiles en el séptimo partido de las Finales de la NBA de 2025.
