articles.title: ‘Might Be Even Better Now,’ ‘Resuming Where He Left Off in Game 7’ — NBA World Raves As Tyrese Haliburton Shines in 1st Return to OKC Since 2025 Finals
articles.summary: The Indiana Pacers fell 114-112 to the Oklahoma City Thunder in overtime on Tuesday, marking their second consecutive preseason loss. However, the result was...
articles.body:
The Indiana Pacers fell 114-112 to the Oklahoma City Thunder in overtime on Tuesday, marking their second consecutive preseason loss.

However, the result was not the biggest talking point. Instead, Tyrese Haliburton stole the spotlight with an impressive performance in his first game against the team that defeated Indiana in the 2025 NBA Finals since returning from injury.

NBA World Amazed by Tyrese Haliburton's Performance vs. Thunder

In his first game back in Oklahoma City since tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals, Haliburton finished with 24 points on 9-for-14 shooting, including 4-for-6 from 3-point range in just 18 minutes.

He also went 2-for-3 from the free-throw line and added 3 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 blocks. All of his points came in the first half , as the two-time All-Star sat out the second half of the overtime loss.

Haliburton averaged 17.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 8.6 assists per game across 23 games in the 2025 NBA playoffs before suffering his devastating injury setback in Game 7 of the Finals. After his latest performance, some fans pointed out that he has the same fire.

"OK, Tyrese is just resuming where he left off in Game 7," one X user said, whereas another wrote, "Haliburton really might be even better now."

During the 2024-25 campaign, Haliburton averaged 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 9.2 assists per game across 73 starts, shooting 47.3% from the field and 38.8% from 3. He helped lead the Pacers to a 50-32 regular-season record and the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference before guiding them to their first NBA Finals appearance in 25 years.

One fan indirectly suggested that had Haliburton not been injured, the Pacers would have won the championship instead of the Thunder.

"Yea, injury saved Shai [Gilgeous-Alexander's] career; that was a Pacers ring," the account said, whereas another wrote , "So NBA Twitter telling me Shai got a fake ring bet."

While most users were busy reacting to how well Haliburton played, one took a different approach. They suggested that the 26-year-old's preseason performance was exactly how he would have played in Game 7 had he not been injured.

"We're seeing exactly what would've happened in that Game 7," the user said.

Although it remains too early to draw conclusions from a preseason game, Haliburton's shooting efficiency marks a promising sign for Indiana. With him back on the court and thriving, the Pacers will hope his return can help them build momentum before the regular season begins.

articles.title: Rui Hachimura Sends Honest Message to Yuki Kawamura After LA Clippers Exit
articles.summary: On Monday, the Los Angeles Clippers parted ways with Yuki Kawamura. The Clippers confirmed that they waived the point guard ahead of the season opener.Accord...
articles.body:
On Monday, the Los Angeles Clippers parted ways with Yuki Kawamura. The Clippers confirmed that they waived the point guard ahead of the season opener.

According to Hoops Rumors, Kawamura was initially signed to an Exhibit 10 contract, which makes him eligible to earn a $91,000 bonus if he decides to play for the Clippers' G League affiliate, the San Diego Clippers.

The 25-year-old played in two preseason games for the Clippers. He had a forgettable night against the Golden State Warriors but bounced back versus the Toronto Raptors. He scored 10 points and dished four assists in 14 minutes against the Raptors.

Rui Hachimura Sends Message to Yuki Kawamura

GettyRui Hachimura #28 of the LA Clippers reacts during the preseason game between Los Angeles Clippers and Toronto Raptors at Rogers Arena on October 10, 2026 in Vancouver, British Columbia.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Rui Hachimura was asked by Japanese reporter Yoko Miyaji about his thoughts on Yuki Kawamura. Hachimura delivered some sound advice for his compatriot, who has mainly played in the NBA G League.

"He really worked hard during training camp, so I want him to keep that up," Hachimura said via BasketNews . "Also, while chasing your dream is important, you have to make smart decisions. He's already 25 years old, so I want him to keep that in mind as he moves forward."

Kawamura has provided a jolt of energy and fanfare whenever he's on a main roster. He has also played better in the G League but can't seem to find a place in the NBA.

His size remains a disadvantage, so it will be interesting to see what Kawamura's next move will be. He can play in the G League again or possibly return to the B.League, wherein he was a top star.

In 35 G League games in two seasons, Kawamura is averaging 14.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 8.7 assists and 1.0 steals per game on 38.3 percent shooting from the field, 39.3 percent from 3-point range and 81.7 percent from the free-throw line.

As one of Japan's biggest young stars, Yuki Kawamura entered the 2023 NBA draft. He was not selected, but he earned a training camp deal with the Memphis Grizzlies a year later. He signed a two-way contract and appeared in 22 games for the Grizzlies as a rookie.

Kawamura played for the Chicago Bulls last season, though he spent the majority of it in the NBA G League. He became a free agent again this past summer, joining the Indiana Pacers for the Summer League.

The Pacers didn't offer him a contract, but the Los Angeles Clippers signed him to a training camp deal.

articles.title: Elle Duncan hints Sophie Cunningham fans have helped turn the WNBA into a ‘disingenuous space’
articles.summary: Netflix sports anchor Elle Duncan gave her thoughts on covering the WNBA amid recent controversy, and seemingly blamed Sophie Cunningham for the recent ‘cult...
articles.body:
Netflix sports anchor Elle Duncan gave her thoughts on covering the WNBA amid recent controversy, and seemingly blamed Sophie Cunningham for the recent 'culture war.'

Cunningham's comments about trans athletes earlier this year brought widespread attention to the league. Unfortunately, the focus wasn't on the players or the happenings on the court.

As such, Cunningham became the most talked-about figure in the WNBA, and it had very little to do with her abilities as a basketball player.

Elle Duncan suggests Sophie Cunningham supporters have 'reduced' WNBA to a 'culture war'

Speaking with Front Office Sports, Netflix sports analyst and anchor Elle Duncan explained why she feels the WNBA has become a toxic space.

She suggested that the people who have come in off the back of certain figures only to try and politicise the league with no regard for the players or the product have reduced conversation around the WNBA to nothing more than a culture war.

Duncan said: "It's toxic as h***. Have y'all ever been in a toxic relationship? Then you know. The reason it's toxic is because you love it so much, because there are so many incredible things about it. Because there is this community that truly doesn't exist anywhere else, and you know how special it is. To have it reduced to a culture war is disgusting, and it sucks.

"It sucks because it's not getting any better. It sucks because we thought three years ago, when this started, it would die down, they would see themselves out, it would regulate, and we are still here. That's why it's toxic. It's toxic because you cannot say anything without p****** off one faction of the population. You can't praise one person without p****** off the other faction of the population.

"It's a disingenuous space – the people that are talking about the most are not fans and don't care. They are literally there are as opportunists, to be divisive. It's working, and that's why it's toxic, because I love it and hate it all at the same time."

While Duncan didn't mention her by name, it is hard to imagine she is referencing any other player's fanbase other than Sophie Cunningham.

Cunningham has become a darling for conservative media members for her stance against trans athletes, allowing them to infiltrate a conversation they had very little interest in for its sporting matters.

Her influence was so massive that even US President Donald Trump recently mentioned and praised Cunningham, although he inadvertently dismissed her abilities as a basketball player in the process.

articles.title: Flyers’ Rick Tocchet reveals the biggest positive of 8th-straight loss
articles.summary: When the Philadelphia Flyers were swept by the eventual champion Carolina Hurricanes in the second round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season, panic did n...
articles.body:
When the Philadelphia Flyers were swept by the eventual champion Carolina Hurricanes in the second round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs last season, panic did not permeate the fan base. People did not lament the future or demand organizational changes. On the contrary, they celebrated a breakthrough campaign that included a first-round triumph over the Pittsburgh Penguins. Continued growth was anticipated. It would be an understatement to say that Philly has taken a step back .

The Flyers suffered a 3-2 shootout loss versus the Seattle Kraken on Tuesday, falling to 0-5-3 in the early goings of the 2026-27 season. Yikes. They have scored just 10 goals so far, which amounts to a measly 1.14 per game. Double Yikes.

However, if one watched Philadelphia's latest unsuccessful effort, they at least saw a team that showed fight on its home ice.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Trevor Zegras was active, goalie Dan Vladar made some superb saves and the Flyers erased a 2-0 deficit in the third period. There were embers of a victorious squad, but they never fully caught fire. Rick Tocchet is trying to find the bright side amid an abysmal start.

"We're still upset at the last two weeks, but the energy was there," the veteran head coach told reporters after the game, per 97.5 The Fanatic. "I saw a lot of guys digging a little bit harder. But it's got to come naturally with this team. It's got to be part of your DNA. It can't be once in a while."

Like many of his players, Tocchet has experienced a brutal turn of events. The 2023-24 Jack Adams Award winner helped revive a franchise that had not competed in the playoffs in six years, and now he is trying to steer his team to its first W before reaching double-digits in games played. Hockey can be a volatile and cruel sport.

If the Flyers are going to survive this October implosion, they will need Zegras to consistently make an impact. He did so on Tuesday.

"It's the best I've seen Trevor play," Rick Tocchet said. "This is what we need from Trevor, this type of game where he wanted the puck, he was in the corners digging, taking a hit to make a play. That's what he has to do."

Trevor Zegras finished second on Philadelphia with 67 points last season, tallying 41 assists and a career-high 26 goals in 81 games. He tied the score versus the Kraken, so perhaps fans witnessed the beginning of a No. 46 explosion.

It will take a collective effort, though. The Flyers will look for some offense against a Detroit Red Wings team that has its own problems.

articles.body: La lucha por la NBA Cup comenzará el viernes 30 de octubre en Prime Video, con el inicio de la fase de grupos en los mercados de los equipos de la NBA. Inspiración en “End of Ordinary” de Nike: Inspiradas en la colección Standard Issue 2026 de Nike Basketball, las pistas trasladan al parqué la atrevida propuesta de diseño de la colección, creando una imagen cohesionada en toda la liga. Nombres de los equipos a gran escala: Los nombres de los equipos, inspirados en la característica chaqueta de juego de la colección, aparecen reproducidos en ambos lados de cada pista. Identidad del equipo en el centro de la pista: Cada pista incorpora el icono principal del equipo local en el círculo central. Ocho equipos accederán a las rondas eliminatorias. Los cuartos de final y las semifinales se disputarán en las ciudades de los equipos de la NBA, antes de que el torneo culmine con la final de la Emirates NBA Cup, en la que solo habrá un ganador, el viernes 11 de diciembre en el emblemático Hinkle Fieldhouse de Indianápolis.
