articles.title: Bronny, Yaxel, Stephen Curry's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Lakers vs. Warriors Preseason
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors earned a 101-89 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers in a preseason game played at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors earned a 101-89 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers in a preseason game played at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Tuesday night.

While some stars such as the Lakers' Luka Dončić and the Warriors' Draymond Green did not suit up for Tuesday's game, other notable players made an impact, including Stephen Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg for Golden State, and Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler for L.A.

Here is look at the production of some of the most significant players and contributors from Tuesday's matchup:

AJ, Trae Continue to Turn Heads with Wizards 🧙‍♂️

The first half largely belonged to the Lakers, as they entered the break with a 13-point lead on the strength of outscoring the Dubs 34-21 in the second quarter.

Reaves, who scored a game-high 28 points for the Lakers, was paramount in Los Angeles jumping out to that early lead, as he racked up buckets and assists throughout the first half, including some hookups with the team's big acquisition if the offseason in Kessler:

Curry, Lendeborg and Podziemski all played big roles in the Warriors staying in it and ultimately taking control in the second half, though.

Steph appeared to be in midseason form with regard to his three-point shooting stroke, while Lendeborg did a little bit of everything, including saving a ball from going out of bounds and dishing it to Podziemski for the triple:

During the second half, the Warriors cut the deficit to four by outscoring the Lakers 22-13 in the third quarter, and then they put it away in the fourth by outscoring L.A. 29-13.

Of course, both teams gave significant playing time to players who may not see the court so much during the regular season, so the result should perhaps be taken with a grain of salt.

Lendeborg was arguably the biggest bright spot in the game, as the rookie No. 11 overall draft pick filled up the stat sheet and tied for the Warriors' team lead with 17 points.

Notable for the Lakers in a less positive way was the performance of Bronny James, who is embarking on his first NBA season away from his legendary dad, LeBron James, who signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Playing 11 minutes, Bronny missed both of his shot attempts, turned the ball over four times and was a game-worst minus-18 when he was on the court.

Both the Warriors and Lakers will play their final preseason games Friday with Golden State facing the Portland Trail Blazers and Los Angeles facing the Denver Nuggets.

Then, the Warriors and Lakers will clash in their regular-season opener on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Lakers' Walker Kessler Talks Preseason Debut After Blockbuster Trade from Jazz, 'Pretty Nervous'
articles.summary: It may have just been an NBA preseason game, but Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler was a little anxious as he donned purple and gold for the first time.
articles.body:
It may have just been an NBA preseason game, but Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler was a little anxious as he donned purple and gold for the first time.

Tuesday's 101-89 defeat to the Golden State Warriors was not just Kessler's Lakers debut but his first action of any kind in nearly a year.

"I mean, it was a lot of fun being out there again. It's been so long," he said, per The Athletic's Dan Woike . "Before the game, I was actually pretty nervous, to be honest. But getting out there and just playing with the guys, it was a blast. I can't really, you know speak to … I think I have a certain presence on the floor, but I think my teammates around me did a great job of playing defense on the perimeter. I think we shared the ball really well tonight. Just how it was, especially in the first half. It was a lot of fun."

Kessler started and played 16 minutes, finishing with 11 points, nine rebounds and one block. The Lakers were plus-15 with him on the floor.

His performance exemplified why Los Angeles paid such a steep price to acquire him in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz. He was effective around the basket on offense and protected the rim at the other end.

"The word I've used with him, you know, the challenge is just being relentless, just in terms of the motor on both ends," head coach JJ Redick said. "Playing off Luka and AR, you know he's going to have opportunities to playmake in the pocket. That's just the nature of how teams guard those two guys. His stats are going to naturally come just from playing hard."

Aside from simply staying healthy, there's little Kessler can do to assuage the concerns about his durability. In terms of his on-court fit with Los Angeles, the early returns are encouraging.

The Lakers close out the preseason on Friday against the Denver Nuggets. They'll tip off the regular season against the Warriors on Oct. 21.

articles.title: SEC accuses LSU of defying its rules as Will Wade’s basketball roster adds fuel to a burning fire
articles.summary: The LSU Tigers filed a motion to dismiss, but the SEC fired back alleging school and Will Wade keep testing conference professionalism rules.
articles.body: A legal battle between the LSU Tigers athletic department and the Southeastern Conference continues to play out in the Northern District Court of Alabama, with an explosive filing on Tuesday evening. If the SEC has its way, the case will linger until LSU acknowledges that it attempted to skirt the conference’s professionalism rules by recruiting — and potentially signing — athletes with professional experience in the NFL or NBA, or until LSU accepts some type of punishment without using a courtroom as a shield. The ongoing saga between one of the SEC’s biggest schools and the conference it resides in has pushed both sides toward a war over the limits of what LSU is permitted to do under league rules. INISDE A LOUISIANA COURTROOM: SEC-LSU LEGAL CIRCUS PLAYED OUT OUT LIKE A JOHN GRISHAM NOVEL IN STUNNING SHOWDOWN Dating back to before the college football season started, multiple athletes at first sued the NCAA for an additional year of eligibility based off the new guidelines that were enacted over how many years an athlete can play collegiate sports. When passed in June, the NCAA made it clear that while athletes would now have five years to play five seasons, they left out the 2022 class. This has led to a plethora of lawsuits being filed across the country, as some judges are granting athletes an additional season based on the NCAA's lack of grandfathering in the 2022 class, while the NCAA has been hellbent to fight each case presented in front of a local judge for consideration. But after a Louisiana district court judge ruled that Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris were eligible to play this season following their professional football experience, the SEC and other conferences adopted a rule barring athletes with professional experience from returning to college sports. LSU MIGHT HAVE TO SUE THE SEC IF THIS LEGAL WAR IS EXPEDITED, WHILE DABO SWINNEY IS STAYING IN HIS 'LANE' This led to attorneys for the plaintiffs adding the SEC to the ongoing lawsuit in a Baton Rouge court, which ultimately saw commissioner Greg Sankey taking the witness stand for over five hours on that Thursday before LSU would take the field against Clemson. It was not 20 minutes into his testimony that word started leaking from within the courtroom that the SEC had filed its own lawsuit against LSU, Lane Kiffin, President Wade Rousse and others within the Tigers administration for encroaching on their first amendment rights to govern themselves within the conference. LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN If you were wondering why the SEC thought it would be best to file this type of lawsuit against a member institution, the conference is working under the impression that LSU would continue using the court system to maneuver around the enforcement of rules. "That threat is not hypothetical. Defendants have already shown they will use Louisiana’s courts to stop the Conference from governing itself," the SEC stated in a filing on Tuesday. "Working hand in glove with the Pyburn plaintiffs, they helped obtain state-court orders that bar the Conference from enforcing the Professionalism Rules." Just like a tale out of a John Grisham novel, the aftermath of that day in Baton Rouge has been nothing short of dramatic. LSU filed motion to dismiss lawsuit, while the SEC hits back with allegations After Lane Kiffin and the Tigers made the decision to not roster both Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, there were some who thought this lawsuit between the two sides would be dropped. "LSU’s eleventh-hour decision not to include two former professional athletes on its football roster does not moot the SEC’s claims," the conference said in a filing on Tuesday. "Nor does it matter that Defendants did not block or interfere with the September 10th meeting." NCAA HAS NO PLANS TO SURRENDER, AS ELIGIBILITY LAWSUITS FOR 2022 CLASS TURN INTO AN ALL-OUT LEGAL WAR But, the fight between LSU and the SEC was essentially just getting started, which also came after subtle threats from the conference to kick the Tigers out of the league. In reality, this was not going to happen, but that hasn’t stopped the SEC from threatening punishment against the Tigers for continuing to recruit athletes with professional experience. Late Tuesday night, in a response to the SEC's response, Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill called the SEC's lawsuit "garbage". "The new response by SEC lawyers proves that the Commissioner was never acting in good faith," AG Murrill said. "LSU has broken no rules, and the case is moot. The lawsuit was garbage from the start and should be dismissed." While some were paying attention to what Lane Kiffin was doing with the football program, the real fight was already starting with LSU basketball coach Will Wade. Kiffin's roster moves were never the real threat in this battle, but more so how the Tigers were putting together a roster for the upcoming basketball season. It was never about football. The entire saga centered around college basketball Just a week ago, LSU technically had just four players on the current roster who were eligible, which came after former St. John's star RJ Luis Jr. was granted an injunction to play college basketball this season, though he has not been added to the Tigers roster. In their strategy to piece together a team, Will Wade has focused a majority of his time on players with professional experience, which was part of the SEC's filing on Tuesday in opposition of LSU's motion to dismiss. "LSU has openly recruited former NBA player RJ Luis Jr., has allowed him to practice with LSU’s men’s basketball team, and has refused to publicly and definitively state that he will not be included on LSU’s basketball roster, which is not due for several more weeks," the SEC's motion stated. For some minds, this strategy is of the same playbook that Lane Kiffin toyed with in the days leading up to LSU's season opener against Clemson. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE LSU LEAVES FORMER PRO-ATHLETES OFF FINAL ROSTER, ONE NIGHT BEFORE SEC TAKES LANE KIFFIN AND TIGERS TO COURT On Tuesday, Will Wade mentioned that LSU would follow the orders set forth by the SEC. "We're going to follow all the SEC protocols with him," Wade said Tuesday during SEC Media Days. "I think it's been pretty clear what the SEC protocols are on all that. He didn't travel with us to McNeese, and he hasn't been rostered." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! While this might please some, the official roster does not have to be submitted until one day before the first game of the regular season., and there are still a handful of players LSU awaits answers on who have some type of professional experience. And, while there might not be any further movement from the football side of things, Will Wade and LSU administrators are still testing the limits of what is allowed by conference standards, at least according to the SEC. "Defendants’ threatened interference with the SEC’s First Amendment freedoms is ongoing," the SEC mentioned. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Now, we wait on a judge in Alabama to rule on whether this case moves forward. But remember, this was always about Will Wade, not Lane Kiffin's football team.

articles.title: Brandon Miller Wants Close to Max Extension From Hornets
articles.summary: Brandon Miller wants to get paid.
articles.body:
According to NBA insider Jake Fischer of Bleacher Report , Brandon Miller is seeking a max contract extension from the Charlotte Hornets .

Miller is eligible for a five-year, $275 million deal.

If the Hornets and Miller can't agree to an extension, Miller will become a restricted free agent next offseason.

Miller appeared in 65 games for the Hornets last season, his third year in the NBA. He averaged 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game while shooting 43.5% from the field, 38.3% from beyond the arc and 89.2% from the free-throw line.

The Hornets open the 2026-27 season on the road against the Brooklyn Nets. The home opener is against the Atlanta Hawks.

Miller enters this season with career averages of 19.0 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. He was the second overall pick in the 2023 draft.

Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges in the offseason, so Miller's usage rate will be high this season. Head coach Charles Lee is widely expected to start Coby White, Miller, Kon Knueppel, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté.

That's a strong starting five on paper for Lee, who is looking to lead the Hornets franchise to the playoffs for the first time since 2016.

The Hornets never made the playoffs with Ball and Bridges leading the way. It's time to see if Miller and Knueppel can do what Ball and Bridges failed to accomplish.

Even though Knueppel didn't win the 2025-26 Rookie of the Year award, he still had a special season for the Hornets. The swingman averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game and shot 47.5% from the field, 42.5% from beyond the arc and 86.3% from the free-throw line. He led the NBA in 3-pointers.

Many Hornets fans are excited to watch Reid play. Reid won the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year award. He enters this season with regular-season averages of 11.9 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game and playoff averages of 10.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.

For Minnesota last season, Reid averaged 13.6 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game while shooting 45.6% from the field, 36.2% from beyond the arc and 73.2% from the free-throw line. He recorded six double-doubles.

Miller and Knueppel are the new franchise players in Charlotte with Ball and Bridges gone. Both forwards have a lot of untapped potential and it will be interesting to see how Reid meshes with the youngsters.

articles.title: Senators hilariously troll itself with Chris Paul meme amid Blues blowout
articles.summary: It was not the best showing for the Ottawa Senators against the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night during the NHL’s Frozen Frenzy. The Blues had been mired in...
articles.body:
It was not the best showing for the Ottawa Senators against the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night during the NHL's Frozen Frenzy. The Blues had been mired in offensive woes , but that was not the case in this game. St. Louis found the back of the net seven times in the 7-2 victory.

With less than two minutes left in the game, Fabian Zetterlund scored on the power play for the Senators, making it a five-goal deficit. Despite the massive blowout, the Senators' social media team took time to celebrate Zetterlund's goal and also troll themselves .

Instead of posting a video of the goal next to a small video of Zetterlund, they put a screenshot of a Chris Paul highlight. The highlight is an internet meme dating back to Game 7 of the 2022 NBA Western Conference Semifinals. Paul was playing for the Phoenix Suns at the time and visiting the Dallas Mavericks. With 7:15 left in the fourth, Paul hit a three, cutting the lead to 107-65.

It was a dreadful game for the Sens on Tuesday night. They gave up a shorthanded goal to Pius Suter in the first period, before giving up goals to Jake Neighbours and Mason McTavish in the second period. In between the Neighbours and McTavish goals, Claude Giroux scored his first goal of the season for the Sens. Suter scored his second of the game in the third, and then Neighbours, McTavish, and Adam Jiricek added three more goals in two minutes to put the Senators down by six.

While it was a rough game for the Sens, they can still celebrate the solid start to the season. The Senators are 5-2-0 on the year, tying them with the Boston Bruins for the best mark in the Atlantic Division. They return to the ice Thursday night to host the New York Islanders.

articles.title: Tim Connelly calls out cowardly peers afraid to take big trade swings
articles.summary: Minnesota Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly is one of the NBA’s best-known basketball executives. Connelly has a history of savvy...
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly is one of the NBA's best-known basketball executives. Connelly has a history of savvy moves that define his resume, including trading for Aaron Gordon and helping build the Denver Nuggets that won the 2023 NBA Finals. He's also made several savvy moves for the Minnesota Timberwolves, including orchestrating the trade that brought Rudy Gobert to the team and building the core that led to two Western Conference Finals runs.

In a recent interview with The Athletic , he criticized his fellow basketball executives for not taking big swings to build teams that could compete for a championship.

"If it doesn't work and it's my job, I'll get fired. That's fine. But I don't ever want to be in a position where we're reluctant to take big swings."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

He believes many fellow basketball executives are afraid to take risks and face heavy media scrutiny.

"My industry has become so risk-averse," Connelly said. "They're so concerned about real-time analysis (from the media). … In all reality, either you're trying to win, or you're chasing that…Occasionally you can rebuild in the years that present itself when you have a (Victor) Wembanyama or someone like that. But the frustrating thing about our league right now is that too many teams are trying to survive and trying to be in between."

He believes you don't stop building the best team until you hoist the Larry O'Brien Trophy.

"Until you win the championship, you've just got to keep shuffling cards," Connelly said. "I don't think we can be fear-driven. One of the few upticks of having a team that doesn't have the proudest history is you shouldn't be afraid to swing."

articles.title: Michigan State basketball forward starting to get NBA draft buzz
articles.summary: One Michigan State player is starting to get his name mentioned more often in NBA draft circles
articles.body:
While I cover Michigan State basketball and football for this website, I have a personal passion for the NBA. I love the NBA, and I also enjoy consuming NBA mock drafts in the offseason, which also helps inform me about different players to keep an eye on during the college basketball season. For over a year now, I have heard Jordan Scott's name mentioned with increasing frequency.

In a recent mock draft with CBS Sports' Adam Finkelstein , Sam Vecenie added, as an honorable mention, that he is 'hearing' good things about Michigan State basketball forward Jordan Scott.

Personally, I have felt that Scott will be an NBA player someday since his first minutes in green and white. At 6-foot-8, with a clean shooting stroke, impressive defensive acumen, and an overall great feel for the game, Scott is everything modern NBA teams seem to covet in their players.

For MSU fans reading this who might be concerned that Scott could jump to the NBA after this season, at least at this time, that shouldn't be a major concern. I still haven't seen Scott listed in any official mock drafts; his name just gets brought up as someone to keep an eye on. However, if he has a strong season, don't be surprised if he starts to get some major attention from NBA teams.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream will play WNBA Finals Game 3, Game 4 at State Farm Arena
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream will play Game 3 and Game 4 of the WNBA Finals games at State Farm Arena, league sources told Channel 2 sports director Zach Klein.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream will play WNBA Finals Game 3 and Game 4 at State Farm Arena, league sources told Channel 2 sports director Zach Klein.

The Dream later confirmed the move with a statement released Tuesday afternoon.

The Dream worked with State Farm Arena, the Atlanta Hawks, Golden State Valkyries, WNBA and NBA to rearrange the schedule. The original plan was to host the games at Gateway Center before all sides came together.

Game 3 will now be played on Wednesday, Oct. 21 instead of Thursday, Oct. 22 due to the Sombr concert. Game 4 will be still held on Saturday, but at 1 p.m.

After Game 4, the Hawks will play their 2026 home opener against the Houston Rockets at 8:30 p.m. Tickets for both games will go on sale at 10 a.m.

Atlanta plays Golden State Valkyries in its first final appearance since 2013. It's a best-of-7 series. Game 1 and Game 2 will be at the Chase Center on Saturday, Oct. 17 and Monday, Oct. 19.

articles.title: Giannis Explains Importance of Changing Jersey Number After Heat Trade from Bucks in New Video
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo reiterated his belief a new number should accompany his change of scenery this offseason.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo reiterated his belief a new number should accompany his change of scenery this offseason.

The two-time MVP appeared on his brother's podcast, the Thanalysis Show , and explained why he's wearing No. 7 instead of No. 34 with Miami.

Antetokounmpo said he "had to get closure" after wrapping up his 13-year run on the Milwaukee Bucks. He did, however, leave the door open for switching back to 34.

This matches what the star forward told reporters during his introductory press conference.

"The reason that I really changed my number is because I feel like 34 holds so much weight and has so much history, and out of respect to the organization that drafted me and I played for for 13 years, I decided to leave that number there and try to start a new chapter," he said in July. "Hopefully, I can leave my mark here in Miami and make No. 7 as legendary as No. 34."

Stars will often change numbers through sheer necessity. The jersey was retired or already in circulation with somebody else on the roster.

Neither of those things was a hurdle for Antetokounmpo. A Heat player hasn't worn No. 34 since Ray Allen from 2012-14, and only three others in franchise history have been assigned the jersey.

But it's understandable why, given how much he achieved on the Bucks, Giannis wants No. 34 to be synonymous with his Milwaukee tenure.
